links.outcome: LLM answer accuracy on hepatitis C guideline questions with vs without guideline context (RAG)
links.effect: Accuracy rose from 43% to 99% (p < 0.001) when guidelines were provided as context in a coherent text corpus with non-text sources converted to text.
links.quote: The results showed a significant improvement in accuracy from 43 to 99% (p < 0.001), when guidelines were provided as context in a coherent corpus of text and non-text sources were converted into text.

unlisted_practices: Reformatting guidelines (converting non-text sources such as tables/flowcharts to text) before LLM ingestion
Few-shot learning prompt engineering (did not improve overall accuracy)

screen.reason: The study tests the impact of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and specific guideline formatting/in-context prompting safeguards to an existing LLM (GPT-4 Turbo) versus baseline without RAG/context.
